To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
negative language related ERPs reflect precision weighted prediction errors.

the amplitude of language related ERP components can be accounted for by a neurobiologically grounded predictive coding architecture, and that this framework has the potential to provide a unified account of the N400 family of components.

negative language related event-related potential (ERP) responses reflect precision weighted prediction error, i.e. error weighted by the relevance (precision) of the information source that leads to the error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a neurobiologically grounded account of language related ERP components, such as the N300, N400 and LAN, and their functional significance in language processing.
the development of a neurobiologically grounded model of language related negative ERP components.
a theoretical framework that allows for the interpretation of negative language related event related potentials (ERP) components as precision weighted prediction error (PPE) signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N400 amplitude reflects a precision weighted prediction error that can be related to the relevance of the linguistic feature leading to the error.
N400 is not a single component.
the N400 is a neurophysiological correlate of the precision weighted prediction error signal that arises when a word does not conform to the expectations of a language user.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N400 is a negative ERP component which is elicited in response to unexpected words, and which reflects the updating of internal models in response to unexpected linguistic information.
the N400 is a neurobiologically and cognitively plausible index of prediction error and precision weighted model updating.
the N400 reflects an error signal, which is weighted by the precision of the information source, which in turn is determined by the cue validity of the information source in the language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N400 and related components are not only sensitive to the semantic and syntactic properties of a stimulus, but also to the precision of the stimulus.
the N400 can, in fact, be related to a neurobiologically grounded account of language, and that such an account can be used to integrate a broad range of N400 literature.
negative ERP components such as N400 are not only relevant in the study of language, but also provide a window to the brain’s predictive machinery.
